A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Aurora and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Shared methods and results can be matched reliably across the expanded evaluations, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting results on TimeMMD, TSFM-Bench and ProbTS, together with component ablations, sampling analysis and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds EPF and TFB evaluations, further baseline comparisons, ablations and visual case analyses.

M1.justification: The reported encoder depth changes from 3 layers in v1 Table 7 to 1 in v3 Table 8. This is a limited architectural configuration revision; Section 3's attention mechanisms, prototype retrieval, loss and sampling procedure remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain whether the revision reflects retraining or a correction.

E1.justification: v3 adds short-term evaluation on five EPF electricity-price datasets and the broad univariate TFB collection spanning yearly-to-hourly and other frequencies. It also adds NYSE deterministic and ILI probabilistic evaluations. These substantially extend the represented data and forecasting scenarios beyond v1's coverage.

E2.justification: TTM joins the retained TSFM-Bench comparison in v3 Tables 2 and 13. New comparisons also evaluate supervised deterministic methods such as TimeKAN, AMD, TimeXer and PatchTST, classical LR/RF baselines on TFB, and small unimodal baselines on TimeMMD (Tables 10–11 and 15–16).

E3.justification: Added protocols include EPF's 168-step input and 24-step output, TFB evaluation using MASE/msMAPE, and additional 10%/20% downstream training comparisons. Figure 9 introduces timing with batch size 64. A.6 also revises the reported model size from 418.6M to 210.8M parameters; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original component ablations and sampling curve are retained. v3 adds tests of prototype-bank size, modality combinations, individual modality guiders and removal of W (Tables 17–19). Appendix C adds history/future, prototype and attention case studies, while Figure 9 extends efficiency analysis across datasets.

E5.justification: v3 introduces forecast bands labeled '80% Confidence Interval' in Figures 15–21, without specifying their construction. The 100-sample CRPS estimation remains unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seed information or uncertainty intervals for aggregate benchmark scores.

E6.justification: Existing forecasting-error entries are retained, but v3 adds substantial benchmark, baseline, ablation and case-study results. For example, Tables 10–11 newly report TFB mean MASE/msMAPE of 2.134/19.964 for Aurora and 2.158/20.096 for Sundial. These are additional results, rather than demonstrated performance gains over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The method equations (1–25), metric definitions (26–29) and mathematical content of Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional formal theorems or proofs; v3's new analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list extend the explicit state-of-the-art claim from three named benchmarks to five, adding TFB and EPF. The central contributions—multimodal zero-shot forecasting, modality-guided attention and prototype-guided probabilistic generation—remain the same.

C2.justification: v1 gives a general explanation that modality guidance focuses attention on useful historical tokens. v3 Figures 18–21 add case-specific interpretations linking stronger patch relationships to relevant trend transitions. No substantive new discussion of limitations or failure boundaries is added.

D1.justification: A.1 newly documents dataset-specific point counts and sources, GPT4-based quality checking, manual sampling and additional prompt examples. A.4 adds baseline-context details, and A.6 revises model configurations. v3 also adds explicit code/checkpoint release information and GitHub/Hugging Face links, materially expanding provenance and reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including TTM, TimeXer, iTransformer, FLAME and SRSNet, removes MagicScaler, and expands appendix background to other time-series analysis tasks. The central positioning against unimodal foundation models and supervised multimodal models remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most introduction and method prose is retained. Local revisions include a shorter conclusion, expanded corpus and related-work explanations, new short-term/showcase/analytics sections, and ethics and reproducibility statements. The related-work appendix moves from C to E, without wholesale restructuring of the main narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial visual material: benchmark and timing charts, a prototype-bank montage, forecast plots, attention heatmaps and comparison/ablation tables. The corpus figure gains source/count columns, and the prompt figure expands from one example to four. Algorithm 1 is relocated; Table 20 redisplays existing TimeMMD zero-shot results.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of Aurora's generality and component contributions. Short-term evaluations broaden applicability, Tables 15–16 and 21 add supervised and downstream-data-fraction comparisons, and Tables 17–19 isolate modality, attention and prototype-capacity effects that v1 did not test separately. Expanded corpus provenance and release documentation also improve assessability and reproducibility. The unexplained configuration revision and absent aggregate run uncertainty limit interpretation, but do not outweigh these gains. The improvement concerns stronger evidence and documentation, rather than an established cross-version accuracy or efficiency gain.
